evidence.paraphrase: Śaunaka asks location and manifestation date. Sūta places Vakratunda at the eastern limit, installed by gods/sages/Gaṇas, manifest on Bhādra bright fourth; midday worship gives immense siddhis, beginning/end less. Images lie in each island/region’s east; square field ten yojanas, deity central with Siddhi left/Buddhi right, lion in front, eight siddhis in eight directions, eight Gaṇas and Śiva/Viṣṇu/Sun/Śakti in four directions.

evidence.paraphrase: Ṛcīka sees fierce radiance in his wife and asks about Kṣatriya potency. She admits the exchange; he predicts her brother will be an ascetic, her son a fierce bowman. Afraid, she asks a Brahmin son and threatens her life otherwise. He shifts that quality to her grandson, informs Viṣṇu of the pregnancy and effects it through tapas. Jamadagni is born to him; Rāma, best bearer of weapons, becomes Jamadagni’s son. Gādhi’s queen bears Viśvāmitra in ninth month; Gādhi installs his grown son in the kingdom and leaves for austerity.

evidence.paraphrase: Viśvāmitra abandons kingdom, fasts and repeats Gāyatrī by puraścaraṇa for Brahminhood, scorching the world. At10,000 years Brahmā offers a boon; his Brahminhood request is answered with further austerity. Brahmā comes ten times offering another boon, which he refuses. His tapas subjects gods and awes Brahmins into assent to his claimed Brahmarṣi rank; Vasiṣṭha still calls him Rājarṣi. Furious, he repeatedly attempts Vasiṣṭha’s death without success and remains distressed.

narrative_events.details: Śaunaka asks location and manifestation date. Śeṣa/Nāga kings, Gandharvas, mountains, Siddhas, Apsarases, Vidyādharas and Kinnaras serve joyfully and exchange Vakratunda stories; bathing in the ocean they create tīrthas bearing their names.

Sūta limits his account: even Śeṣa, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Vedas, Skanda and yogins cannot exhaust it, and he repeats Mudgala’s account to Dakṣa.

Bhārgava sage Ṛcīka grows old through long austerity, sees deer with mates/descendants, desires household life and asks king Gādhi’s daughter. Gādhi demands a thousand dark-eared horses as his established marriage-price. Ṛcīka gets them from Varuṇa and gives them; frightened Gādhi duly marries his daughter to him. Her mother laments, provides goods/clothes and sends her to the forest, where she diligently serves Ṛcīka.

Pleased by his wife’s good conduct, Ṛcīka uses his own austerity to create a richly adorned forest city with four social classes, servants and wealth, and adopts a youthful form. He enjoys marriage properly, then judges its pleasures small and becomes unattached.

The queen visits with wealth/clothes and finds a magnificent city rather than the hermitage; a sweeper identifies Ṛcīka’s city and summons her daughter. Seeing the prosperous sage, she tells her daughter to ask him for sons for both women. Ṛcīka prepares two carus/puroḍāśas with Brahmin/Kṣatriya potency and specifies each eater, then leaves for midday rites. The mother orders exchanging their portions; daughter complies, mother returns home, both become pregnant.

Ṛcīka sees fierce radiance in his wife and asks about Kṣatriya potency. She admits the exchange; he predicts her brother will be an ascetic, her son a fierce bowman. Afraid, she asks a Brahmin son and threatens her life otherwise. He shifts that quality to her grandson, informs Viṣṇu of the pregnancy and effects it through tapas. Jamadagni is born to him; Rāma, best bearer of weapons, becomes Jamadagni’s son. Gādhi’s queen bears Viśvāmitra in ninth month; Gādhi installs his grown son in the kingdom and leaves for austerity.

King Viśvāmitra hunts, grows hungry/thirsty and reaches Vasiṣṭha’s hermitage. Vasiṣṭha feeds king and army by the cow’s power. Viśvāmitra requests Nandinī; refused, he orders her seizure. She destroys the messengers; when men whip her, she creates a great army which destroys the king’s whole army. He returns defeated.

Viśvāmitra leaves rule to ministers and propitiates Śaṅkara in forest. At100 years Śiva grants complete missile knowledge. He returns, attacks Vasiṣṭha and hermitage with fire missile and other weapons. Vasiṣṭha’s Brahmadaṇḍa destroys every missile and defeats him; he flees. Brahmins comfort Vasiṣṭha. Viśvāmitra recognizes Brahmin power’s superiority and his destroyed weapons.

Viśvāmitra abandons kingdom, fasts and repeats Gāyatrī by puraścaraṇa for Brahminhood, scorching the world. At10,000 years Brahmā offers a boon; his Brahminhood request is answered with further austerity. Brahmā comes ten times offering another boon, which he refuses. Yājñavalkya, explicitly arisen from Brahmā’s limb, visits. Viśvāmitra bows, worships and says birth, study and austerity bear fruit through seeing him; he asks the visit’s purpose and offers obedience as his servant.
